newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan aluminium demand seen up 3 pct in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Japan aluminium demand seen up 3 pct in 1997/98.

text.p: Japan's demand for fabricated aluminium products is expected to rise three percent in the fiscal year beginning in April 1997, the chairman of the Japan Aluminum Federation said on Monday.

"Speaking about the next fiscal year, if aluminium for automobiles stays at the prior year's levels, we think growth (in demand) will be about three percent, lifted by flat-rolled products," Masahiro Kumamoto told a news conference.

He reiterated his scepticism, however, about recent statements from the government that Japan's economy was recovering, adding that the federation expected the economy to grow by about one percent or less in 1997/98.
He also said the recent sharp drop in Tokyo share prices contributed to extreme uncertainty in the economic outlook.
Referring to the stock market's declines and the yen's weakening against the dollar, he said, "I share the view that these are (the result of) worries about the Japanese economy."
He urged the government to take action to stimulate the economy even as it adopts measures, such as an April hike in the national sales tax, to curtail government debt.
"Personally, I feel that improving the government's finances without measures to boost the economy would be extremely difficult," he said.
